text.t: Collagen is three protein chains wound together into a tight triple helix.
This is a short lab-made piece of 30 amino acids per chain; a real collagen chain is over 1400 amino acids long.
Each chain repeats the same three amino acids again and again: proline, hydroxyproline, glycine.
Every third amino acid is glycine, a small amino acid that fits neatly into the crowded centre of the helix.
Hydroxyproline is proline with an extra oxygen added after the chain is built, a step that needs vitamin C.
In this crystal hydroxyprolines help hold a sleeve of water molecules around the helix.
Here the researchers put a bigger alanine where a glycine should be.
It crowds the neighbouring chains and makes the helix untwist a little at that spot.

does.t: Collagen is a major structural protein that forms cables in tendons and tough sheets that support skin and internal organs.
Bones and teeth are made by adding mineral crystals to collagen.
About one quarter of all the protein in your body is collagen.

shape.t: Three long chains twist around each other like the strands of a rope, forming a sturdy molecular cable.
Glycine at every third position tucks into the tight centre, while proline and hydroxyproline bend each chain smoothly around the helix.
Type I collagen molecules line up side by side, like fibers in a rope, to build tough fibrils between our cells.

text.t: Collagen sits outside cells, filling the space between nearly all of them.
Hemoglobin is a round, globular protein, but collagen in the skin is a long, fibrous one.

wrong.t: Without enough vitamin C, the body cannot make hydroxyproline, new collagen stops being built, and the result is scurvy.
Loose teeth and easy bruising in scurvy come from missing collagen repairs.
Changes of a glycine to another amino acid in collagen are linked to diseases such as osteogenesis imperfecta and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV.

history.who: J. Bella, M. Eaton, B. Brodsky and H.M. Berman

text.t: This X-ray study of a collagen-like peptide showed a protein triple helix atom by atom at 1.9 angstroms.
It confirmed the basic triple-helix shape that earlier studies of collagen fibers had predicted.

compare.t: This short piece of collagen is about 8.7 nm long from end to end.
Each chain here has 30 amino acids, while a full collagen chain has over 1400, so a whole molecule is far longer.

text.t: This alanine replaces a glycine and locally untwists the triple helix.
Glycine sits at every third position, inside the helix.
Hydroxyproline needs vitamin C to be made.
